findings.summary: Document language is encoded as en_GB, which is not a valid BCP 47 language tag.
findings.fix: In Acrobat Pro, open File > Properties > Advanced > Reading Options and set Language to English (UK). Verify that the saved catalog /Lang is en-GB. Test pronunciation with a screen reader.
findings.evidence: Catalog object 186: /Lang (en_GB); BCP 47 uses hyphens, so British English is en-GB. Invalid syntax is confirmed; reader fallback or mispronunciation was not tested.

findings.summary: The meaningful version and publication date are untagged and absent from the logical structure.
findings.fix: In Acrobat Pro, open the Tags and Reading Order panels and tag "Version 1.0, June 2026" as a paragraph before the title. Check tag order and screen-reader output. In the source document, place this information in the main reading flow before exporting again.
findings.evidence: Page 1 stream draws "Version 1.0, June 2026" before the first /H1 marked-content block, without any enclosing tag or Artifact marker. The tag tree starts with the title and has no version/date entry.

findings.summary: PDF/UA structure: 36 of 37 list items contain content directly instead of an LBody child.
findings.fix: In Acrobat Pro, use the Tags panel to move each item body into LBody under its LI, and separate visible bullets or numbers into Lbl where appropriate. Preserve each split item as one logical item, then validate with PAC or veraPDF.
findings.evidence: Ten L elements contain 37 LI elements. Only LI object 101 has an LBody child; the other 36 have direct MCIDs/MCRs. No Lbl elements exist. Lists and item counts are present; a WCAG relationship failure or screen-reader navigation failure was not established.

passed: Document has a StructTreeRoot, Document root and /MarkInfo /Marked true.
Title metadata is "Wagtail Product Strategy 2026 v1.0" and /DisplayDocTitle is true.
All 11 pages contain extractable text; all four fonts are embedded and have ToUnicode mappings. Ligature ActualText replacements are present.
Fifteen descriptive heading bookmarks point to destinations; heading tags use H1 and H2 without skipped levels.
All five URI link annotations are represented by Link tags and OBJR references, with visible descriptive text (WCAG, ATAG, Web Sustainability Guidelines, The Zen of Wagtail, OWASP Top 10).
All 11 pages specify /Tabs /S. There are no form fields, scripts, encryption or image-only pages.
Visual inspection of rendered pages 1-11 found a single-column text layout, no charts or tables, no clipped content and visibly underlined links. No image XObjects were found.
Measured vector text colors on a white background: body gray RGB 0.2824/0.2824/0.2824 has 9.14:1 contrast; link blue RGB 0.0667/0.3333/0.8 has 6.57:1 contrast. Both exceed 4.5:1.
notes: Source: https://media.wagtail.org/documents/Wagtail_Product_Strategy_2026_v1.0.pdf. Audit target: WCAG 2.2 AA; strict checks, including separately identified PDF/UA and best-practice observations. No workspace PDF configuration or previous document audit was provided.

Tools: Poppler pdfinfo/pdftotext/pdftoppm/pdffonts 26.08.0, qpdf 12.4.1, Python standard-library JSON inspection, ImageMagick contact-sheet rendering. Reviewed all 11 rendered pages and catalog, tags, fonts, outlines, annotations, page tab settings and decompressed content streams.

Limitations: veraPDF and PAC were unavailable, and no Acrobat accessibility checker or screen-reader runtime test was performed. This is a structural and visual audit, not a full WCAG or PDF/UA certification. Test tag-based reading order, list navigation, link keyboard activation, pronunciation and reflow in Acrobat with NVDA or another screen reader. Text extraction alone does not prove accessible reading order.

PDF/UA-only observation: no XMP metadata stream or pdfuaid:part identifier is present. This PDF makes no machine-readable PDF/UA conformance claim; absence of that claim is not itself a WCAG failure. If PDF/UA delivery is required, repair structure, add suitable metadata and validate the actual result with veraPDF/PAC before asserting conformance.

Heading review: the title and five major section headings are all H1 (six total); nine subsections are H2. A single H1 title followed by H2 sections and H3 subsections would make the hierarchy clearer, but multiple H1 tags alone do not establish a WCAG failure. Confirm the intended outline with the author.

Reference for list structure: https://pdfa.org/wp-content/until2016_uploads/2015/12/StructureElementsBestPracticeGuide_2016-01-19.pdf and https://pac.pdf-accessibility.org/en/resources/quality-checks/formal-correctness-of-li-elements. Language syntax: https://www.w3.org/International/articles/language-tags/Overview.en.php. Project PDFUA rule identifiers are used for traceability; they are not a completed Matterhorn validator result.
